blocks.text: DAT:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Data affordance block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 125 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 24 complete Data-family soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: DAT:2xx names substrate-neutral affordances enabling the canonical DAT:1xx processes. The inward triplet names represented information’s capacity for bounded transformation within one entity; the outward triplet names one source context’s information-transfer relation to one distinct target; and the systemic triplet names capacity for coordinated information-state alignment across multiple participants under one synchronization criterion. The third trit changes only persistent, operative, or latent status.

DAT:200 — persistent internal data transformability — A persistent capacity of represented information within one reference entity to undergo bounded internal data transformation, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.
DAT:201 — operative internal data transformability — A capacity of represented information within one reference entity to undergo bounded internal data transformation that is presently operative.

DAT:202 — latent internal data transformability — A capacity of represented information within one reference entity to undergo bounded internal data transformation that exists without being presently operative.

DAT:210 — persistent source-target data transferability — A persistent information-transfer relation between one source context and one distinct reference target that can enable bounded target data transfer, independently of whether that relation is presently operative.

DAT:211 — operative source-target data transferability — An information-transfer relation between one source context and one distinct reference target that presently enables bounded target data transfer.

DAT:212 — latent source-target data transferability — An information-transfer relation between one source context and one distinct reference target that exists without presently enabling bounded target data transfer.

DAT:220 — persistent systemic data synchronizability — A persistent capacity of information states across multiple participants in one shared data domain to undergo coordinated alignment under one synchronization criterion, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.

DAT:221 — operative systemic data synchronizability — A capacity of information states across multiple participants in one shared data domain to undergo coordinated alignment under one synchronization criterion that is presently operative.

DAT:222 — latent systemic data synchronizability — A capacity of information states across multiple participants in one shared data domain to undergo coordinated alignment under one synchronization criterion that exists without being presently operative.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode the information entity, actual process, physical carrier, storage device, channel, algorithm, resource, observer, or result. Internal transformability does not entail readability, writability, losslessness, understanding, access, or permission. Source-target transferability does not entail a physical path, communicative uptake, delivery, acknowledgment, or persistence. Systemic synchronizability does not entail present agreement, integrity, provenance, consistency, convergence, or restoration. Persistent identity may co-occur with operative or latent status; operative and latent are mutually exclusive at one reference time. Lexical latency remains distinct from runtime [2]/num uncertainty.
